channel.title: Daily Tech Opinions Digest
channel.description: Daily digest of tech opinions and blog posts curated for Yun Zhou

item.title: Bruce Schneier: Bias in Qwen3-Coder Model
item.description: Qwen3-Coder writes measurably more hackable code for a US defense contractor than a Chinese one, and prompting for secure code widens the gap; removing the CCP alignment in the weights closed it.

item.title: Scott Aaronson: Podcasts about the Topic: Part II
item.description: Buried in a podcast roundup: Aaronson says his students report an OpenAI model has now refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis with a roughly exp(n/sqrt(log n)) 3SAT algorithm - unverified, but the next Mathacre-scale claim to watch.

item.title: Torsten Slok (Apollo): The AI Payoff Hasn't Reached Most Companies. Some Raises Slowed Anyway.
item.description: Apollo's Torsten Slok: revenue per worker and margins are rising only for the Mag 7 and flat for the S&P 493, with no productivity sign - yet pay growth in AI-exposed jobs already lagged about 6.7pp since 2023.

item.title: Cory Doctorow: Sovereign citizens, but for news
item.description: The LA Times blocks articles behind a click claiming mere reading waives your right to sue and consents to tracking - Doctorow calls the browsewrap illegal and 'sovereign citizens, but for news.'

item.title: Sebastian Raschka: Build Your Own Reasoning Model: A Full Video Course
item.description: Eleven hours, eight videos, building a reasoning model on Qwen3 0.6B in PyTorch - RLVR/GRPO, inference-time scaling and distillation, code-along.
